quote.text: Externals include the body and its members, as well as material goods. If you grow attached to any of them as if they were your own, you will incur the penalties prescribed for a thief.
quote.author: Epictetus
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood:
    • Recognize that children are not possessions but souls to be nurtured; do not cling to the transient forms of physical affection or material gestures, but invest in their inner virtues.
    • Remember that fostering resilience and character in your children means teaching them to value inner strength over external attachments—a lesson that will guide them through life’s inevitable ups and downs.
  • Leadership:
    • True leadership lies in focusing on the greater good and shared values rather than the lure of power or material gains; let your actions be guided by principles that transcend temporary rewards.
    • Manage your team and responsibilities with a clear mind, understanding that external accolades are fleeting and that integrity and service are what build lasting trust.
  • Product Management:
    • In product management, prioritizing long-term value over short-term material successes encourages innovation and quality, reminding us that the essence of a product lies in its ability to serve and improve lives.
    • Adopt a mindset that scrutinizes attachments to external markers of success, instead investing efforts in creating resilient, user-centered solutions that reflect enduring virtues.
